content.title: About
content.content: Corn, scalloped or pudding is a dish made from whole corn kernels, milk, eggs and sugar, baked until a golden crust forms. In the United States it is often served in the autumn season and is considered a traditional family comfort food in many regions.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn is one of the oldest cultivated crops, domesticated over 7,000 years ago in Mesoamerica.
The baked version is commonly called “corn pudding” or “corn casserole” in English‑speaking countries.
Traditional recipes include milk, cream, and sometimes butter, giving the dish a rich, silky texture.
In some U.S. regions the pudding is served with maple syrup or cinnamon for extra flavor.
Corn’s bright yellow color comes from carotenoids, which have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Corn provides carbohydrates that quickly supply the body with energy.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Source of magnesium and potassium
items.content: These minerals help regulate blood pressure and support muscle function.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Carotenoids and phenolic compounds in corn protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn, ranging from skin rashes to severe symptoms.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Traditional pudding often contains added sugar, which may be unsuitable for people with diabetes or those limiting calories.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: The dish is rich in fats and carbs, so portion control is advisable to avoid over‑consumption.

items.title: Gluten in additives
items.content: Some recipes use flour or starch that contain gluten; gluten‑free alternatives should be used for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Corn pudding can be served warm as a dessert or side dish. Bake it in a casserole dish and enjoy with berry sauce, whipped cream, or ice cream. A chilled version is also refreshing in summer.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared pudding in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat in the microwave or oven as needed. Do not keep at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
